text.en: The regulator said / it needs an / [assessment].

captions.source: LVV (the permit and supervision agency): the Muhos project needs an environmental impact assessment (YVA) on the felled hectares alone (the law's threshold is 200 ha of regeneration felling; 300+ ha was cut) — per the same STT coverage; LVV's 6 Oct order stopped the preparatory work until the assessments are done (AFP, Al Jazeera, Yle). The on-screen email from LVV shows its sender and a subject only: the body is blank bars, because the email's wording is not known.

A Google employee's reply in the released emails, as quoted in the STT coverage: "Kyllä, olemme tietoisia :( Tämä tulee todella viivästyttämään projektiamme" ("Yes, we are aware :( This will really delay our project"). The employee is a private individual and is never named: 'a Google email, released to STT'. The screen shows the Finnish; the caption is the station's translation. QUOTE STATUS: from search summaries (6 Nov 17:16), not re-confirmed on 6–7 Nov; open the STT text and match it word for word before the full build.

About 330 ha was cleared at Muhos before the environmental assessment (Google's own figure; LVV says over 300 ha; Fortune 26 Oct, Kainuun Sanomat, MT, Kaleva). The posted Cut First rests on the same facts. Kaleva/MT also report Tuike Finland asked LVV in April for an exception so permits could be issued before the YVA was complete. The film's order (email, then trees) is shorthand: the email's date relative to the felling is not reported; 'first' means before the assessment.

The station's line: the company knew an assessment was required (the email; its April exception request) and the felling went ahead before it was done. Google's side rides on the tag: it believed the felling could lawfully go ahead under forest-use notices and the building act while the YVA was pending (its response to LVV, SSS, Oct 2026), and its spokesperson denies any unlawful conduct.
